chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'There is nothing between faith and disbelief except a deficiency of intellect.'

It was asked: 'And how is that so, O son of the Messenger of God?' He said: 'Indeed, the servant directs his desire toward a created being, whereas if he had made his intention sincere for God, He would have given him what he desires in a time quicker than that.'

key_terms.الإخلاص: Ikhlas — sincerity of intention, directing one's acts purely for God
key_terms.الإيمان: Iman — faith, conviction, the inner state of belief in God and His messengers
key_terms.الكفر: Kufr — disbelief, rejection, the covering over or denial of truth
key_terms.المخلوق: Makhlūq — a created being; here contrasted with the Creator as an improper object of hope
key_terms.قلة العقل: Deficiency of intellect — not a lack of intelligence, but a failure to apply reason in recognizing the proper object of one's hopes

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between faith, disbelief, and intellect according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that the boundary between iman (faith) and kufr (disbelief) is a deficiency of the intellect. He explains this by pointing to a pattern of misaligned desire: the person who turns to created beings for their needs, rather than directing their sincere intention (niyyah) entirely to God, has not fully realized their faith. This teaching was given in a scholarly gathering context, where a questioner probed the meaning of the statement, and the Imam responded with a practical illustration grounded in the theology of tawakkul (reliance on God) and ikhlas (sincerity).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There isn’t anything between the Eman and the disbelief (Kufr) except for the scarcity of the intellect’.

It was said, ‘And how is that so, O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! The servant raises his desire to the creatures (people). So had he been of sincere intention to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, He<sup>azwj</sup> would Give him that which he wants in (a time period) quicker than that’.
